name: Flow
description: Record a task once with your mouse and keyboard, and Flow repeats it for you. A macro recorder and auto-clicker for Windows.

hero.lede: Record a task once with your mouse and keyboard, and Flow repeats it for you. A macro recorder and auto-clicker in one small file.
notes: If Windows says it protected your PC, click More info, then Run anyway.
hero.away: Flow runs on Windows. Open this page on your PC to download it.

image.name: hero
image.alt: Flow's window with Record, Play and the auto-clicker, a macro of 1098 events loaded

features.label: Record
features.title: Record mouse and keyboard
body: Press <kbd>F8</kbd> and Flow records mouse moves, clicks, wheel scrolling and keystrokes, timed to the microsecond. Its own hotkeys stay out of the recording.

main.name: f1
main.alt: Flow recording, with 310 events in 6.7 seconds

features.label: Playback
features.title: Replay at the speed you need
body: Play a macro at 0.1x to 100x, for 1 to 999 loops or until you stop it. Humanize timing adds a small random variation to each delay.

main.name: f2
main.alt: Flow playing a macro at speed 2 for 5 loops

features.label: Clicker
features.title: Click at a set interval
body: Click every 1 to 10,000 ms with the left, right or middle button, as a single, double or triple click.
Click at the cursor or at a fixed point you drag out from the Target field, and add jitter or a click limit.

main.name: f3
main.alt: The auto-clicker running every 50 ms with a fixed target

features.label: Hotkeys
features.title: Hotkeys that work anywhere
body: <kbd>F8</kbd> records, <kbd>F9</kbd> plays, <kbd>F6</kbd> starts the clicker and <kbd>Pause</kbd> stops everything, also while another window has focus.
Rebind any of them to F1 to F12, A to Z or 0 to 9.

main.name: f4
main.alt: The Customize Hotkeys dialog with F8, F9, F6 and Pause

features.label: Macros
features.title: Save a macro, open it later
body: Save a recording as a .rec file, then open it again or drop it onto the window. With Reopen Last Macro on Launch, Flow loads it when it starts.

main.name: f5
main.alt: The Settings menu with Reopen Last Macro on Launch ticked

new.label: Built 10 October 2026
items: The auto-clicker has its own options: button, single, double or triple click, jitter and a click limit.
Pick a fixed click point by dragging from the Target field.
The window follows each monitor's scale.
Settings save as soon as they change.
The window always opens inside the work area, clear of the taskbar.

requirements: Administrator rights, asked for when it starts
No install and no internet connection

privacy.title: No network at all
body: Flow has no network code and sends nothing anywhere. Your recordings stay in the files you save.

data.title: One settings file
body: Your hotkeys and options live in one plain text file, %APPDATA%\FLOW\settings.cfg. Macros are .rec files, saved only where you choose.

keys_note: All four work in any window and can be changed in Settings, Customize Hotkeys.

basics.title: Get started
steps: Double-click it and click Yes when Windows asks for permission.
Press <kbd>F8</kbd>, do the task once, press <kbd>F8</kbd> again.

basics.title: Updates
body: Close Flow and download the new FLOW.exe over the old one. Your settings stay in %APPDATA%\FLOW.

basics.title: Removing it
body: Close Flow, delete FLOW.exe and the %APPDATA%\FLOW folder, and any .rec files you no longer want.

a: Yes. It is a free download with no account.

faq.q: Why does Windows say it protected my PC?
a: Flow is not signed with a paid certificate, so Windows warns about a new download. Click More info, then Run anyway.
To check that the file is intact, compare its hash with the checksum file: Get-FileHash .\FLOW.exe.

faq.q: Why does Flow ask for Administrator rights?
a: Windows blocks a normal program from sending input to, or recording input from, a window that runs as Administrator, such as Task Manager or an installer. With the rights, Flow works in every window.

faq.q: Where does Flow keep my data?
a: In %APPDATA%\FLOW\settings.cfg. Your macros are only where you save them, and nothing goes over the network.

faq.q: My antivirus flags Flow. Is that a problem?
a: Some engines flag every tool that records and replays input. It is a false positive. The checksum file tells you that you have the released file.

faq.q: Is there a zip instead of the exe?
a: Yes: FLOW-win64.zip holds the same exe and the license.

closing.title: Get Flow
closing.sub: Free for Windows 10 and 11. One file, nothing to install.
